guides.title: A Guide to Disaster Relief Funding Opportunities
guides.intro: Help for New Yorkers before, during, and after a disaster: how to apply for FEMA aid, low-interest SBA loans, farm and community recovery programs, and New York State resources.

items.title: FEMA Individual Assistance (DisasterAssistance.gov)
items.summary: After a presidentially declared disaster that includes Individual Assistance, FEMA can help eligible people with needs not covered by insurance, such as temporary housing and home repairs. DisasterAssistance.gov is the federal government’s single place to apply for FEMA assistance, check the status…
items.html:
After a presidentially declared disaster that includes Individual Assistance, FEMA can help eligible people with needs not covered by insurance, such as temporary housing and home repairs. DisasterAssistance.gov is the federal government’s single place to apply for FEMA assistance, check the status of an application, upload documents, and find other recovery help.

  • Check whether your county is included in a declaration and apply online at DisasterAssistance.gov.
  • Each disaster has an application deadline; disasters with past dates may still accept late applications.
  • If you need help completing your application, call the FEMA Helpline at 1-800-621-3362, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. (your time zone), 7 days a week. If you use a video relay service or captioned telephone, give FEMA the number for that service.

items.title: SBA Home and Personal Property Disaster Loans
items.summary: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) offers low-interest, long-term disaster loans to homeowners and renters in declared disaster areas. You do not need to own a business. Home loans: homeowners may borrow up to $500,000 to repair or replace their primary residence. Personal property loans:…
items.html:
The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) offers low-interest, long-term disaster loans to homeowners and renters in declared disaster areas. You do not need to own a business.

  • Home loans: homeowners may borrow up to $500,000 to repair or replace their primary residence.
  • Personal property loans: homeowners and renters may borrow up to $100,000 to repair or replace personal property such as clothing, furniture, cars, and appliances.
  • Insurance and other recovery payments may be deducted from the eligible loan amount. Second homes and vacation properties are not eligible.
  • Loans may be increased to pay for improvements that reduce future damage, such as retaining walls, sump pumps, and safe rooms.

For more information, visit SBA Disaster Assistance.

Contact: 1-800-659-2955 or disastercustomerservice@sba.gov. TTY users dial 7-1-1.
items.source: SAM.gov Assistance Listing 59.008 (published Feb. 4, 2026, downloaded Nov. 2026); https://www.sba.gov/about-sba/sba-locations/headquarters/office-of-disaster-recovery/ (snapshot 03)

items.title: 203(h) Mortgage Insurance for Disaster Victims and 203(k) Rehabilitation Mortgage Insurance
items.summary: Section 203(h) Mortgage Insurance for Disaster Victims helps people whose homes were destroyed or severely damaged in a presidentially declared disaster area get a mortgage to rebuild or buy another home. No down payment is required, and the borrower may finance 100 percent of the home. You must…
items.html:
Section 203(h) Mortgage Insurance for Disaster Victims helps people whose homes were destroyed or severely damaged in a presidentially declared disaster area get a mortgage to rebuild or buy another home. No down payment is required, and the borrower may finance 100 percent of the home. You must apply through an FHA-approved lender within one year of the disaster declaration.

Section 203(k) Rehabilitation Mortgage Insurance lets you buy or refinance a home that is at least a year old and finance the cost of repairing it in a single mortgage. For repairs that do not require buying or refinancing, HUD’s Title I Property Improvement Loan Program may be an option.

For more information, visit Section 203(h) and Section 203(k).

Contact: 1-800-CALL-FHA (1-800-225-5342), TTY 1-800-877-8339, Answers@hud.gov

items.title: Disaster Unemployment Assistance
items.summary: Disaster Unemployment Assistance provides financial help to people whose job or self-employment was lost or interrupted as a direct result of a major disaster declared by the President, and who are not eligible for regular unemployment insurance. Apply through the New York State Department of Labor…
items.html:
Disaster Unemployment Assistance provides financial help to people whose job or self-employment was lost or interrupted as a direct result of a major disaster declared by the President, and who are not eligible for regular unemployment insurance. Apply through the New York State Department of Labor after a declaration.

For more information, visit the U.S. Department of Labor’s Disaster Recovery Assistance page, or call 1-866-487-2365.

items.title: Disaster Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (D-SNAP) and Disaster Food Help
items.summary: After a disaster, USDA works with the State to provide food assistance: D-SNAP: if stores are open in the affected area, the State may run a Disaster Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program. D-SNAP uses different rules than regular SNAP, so households that would not normally qualify may be…
items.html:
After a disaster, USDA works with the State to provide food assistance:

  • D-SNAP: if stores are open in the affected area, the State may run a Disaster Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program. D-SNAP uses different rules than regular SNAP, so households that would not normally qualify may be eligible because of disaster-related expenses such as home repairs, temporary shelter, evacuation, or lost income. Benefits are loaded on an EBT card.
  • Current SNAP households may be able to get replacement benefits for food lost in the disaster, and in some declared disasters may be allowed to buy hot, prepared foods for a period of time.
  • USDA Foods Disaster Household Distribution: when normal food channels are disrupted, the State may distribute boxes of USDA Foods, usually for two weeks to one month. Families may receive both D-SNAP and a USDA Foods box.

For more information, visit USDA Disaster Assistance.

Contact: New York State SNAP Hotline, 1-800-342-3009
items.source: https://www.fna.usda.gov/disaster (snapshot 15); FNS 'Improving Access and Parity' final rule, Oct. 2024 (via search)

items.title: Home Energy Assistance (HEAP / LIHEAP)
items.agency: HHS / NYS Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance
items.summary: The federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) helps low-income households with home heating and cooling bills, energy crises, and weatherization and minor energy-related repairs. In New York, it is run by the Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance as the Home Energy…
items.html:
The federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) helps low-income households with home heating and cooling bills, energy crises, and weatherization and minor energy-related repairs. In New York, it is run by the Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance as the Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP), which includes emergency benefits for households facing a heating emergency.

For more information, visit NYS HEAP or contact your local Department of Social Services.

items.title: Insurance Help: Flood Insurance and New York State Insurance Assistance
items.agency: FEMA / NYS Department of Financial Services
items.summary: Most homeowners and renters insurance does not cover flood damage. Flood insurance is available separately through FEMA’s National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) for homeowners, renters, and businesses. Report a flood loss right away to your insurance agent or company. Need help finding them? Call…
items.html:
Most homeowners and renters insurance does not cover flood damage. Flood insurance is available separately through FEMA’s National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) for homeowners, renters, and businesses.

  • Report a flood loss right away to your insurance agent or company. Need help finding them? Call the NFIP at 1-877-336-2627 or visit FloodSmart.gov.
  • The New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS) can answer questions about coverage and claims and accepts complaints about insurers. Visit DFS Disaster and Flood Recovery or call the DFS Disaster Hotline at 1-800-339-1759.
  • Before a disaster, keep photos or video of your home and belongings and a copy of your policy in a safe, dry place.

items.title: Disaster Legal Services
items.summary: Disaster Legal Services (DLS) provides free legal help to low-income disaster survivors. FEMA provides this service through an agreement with the Young Lawyers Division of the American Bar Association. DLS may help with insurance claims, replacing wills and other legal papers lost in the disaster,…
items.html:
Disaster Legal Services (DLS) provides free legal help to low-income disaster survivors. FEMA provides this service through an agreement with the Young Lawyers Division of the American Bar Association. DLS may help with insurance claims, replacing wills and other legal papers lost in the disaster, home repair contracts and contractors, problems with landlords, proof of home ownership, and FEMA appeals. DLS attorneys are not FEMA employees, and their services are confidential.

Contact: FEMA Helpline, 1-800-621-3362

items.title: Federal Benefit Payments: Switch from Paper Checks
items.summary: Since September 30, 2025, the federal government has stopped issuing paper checks for most federal payments, including Social Security and veterans benefits, except in very limited circumstances. Electronic payments are safer during a disaster because they do not depend on mail delivery. Direct…
items.html:
Since September 30, 2025, the federal government has stopped issuing paper checks for most federal payments, including Social Security and veterans benefits, except in very limited circumstances. Electronic payments are safer during a disaster because they do not depend on mail delivery.

  • Direct deposit: sign up through the agency that pays your benefits, at GoDirect.gov, or by calling the Electronic Payment Solution Center at 1-800-967-6857 (Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. ET).
  • Direct Express® Debit Mastercard®: a prepaid card for people without a bank account. Cards are now issued by Fifth Third Bank. Visit USDirectExpress.com.

items.summary: Disaster Distress Helpline: call or text 1-800-985-5990 to talk with a trained counselor, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: call, text, or chat 988, 24/7. Free and confidential. SAMHSA National Helpline: 1-800-662-HELP (4357), free, confidential treatment referral, in…
items.html:
• Disaster Distress Helpline: call or text 1-800-985-5990 to talk with a trained counselor, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
  • 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: call, text, or chat 988, 24/7. Free and confidential.
  • SAMHSA National Helpline: 1-800-662-HELP (4357), free, confidential treatment referral, in English and Spanish.
  • Find treatment: FindTreatment.gov

For more information, visit SAMHSA: Find Help.

items.summary: The Administration for Community Living (ACL) offers resources to help older adults, people with disabilities, families, caregivers, and service providers prepare for and respond to emergencies. For more information, visit ACL Emergency Preparedness.
items.html:
The Administration for Community Living (ACL) offers resources to help older adults, people with disabilities, families, caregivers, and service providers prepare for and respond to emergencies.

For more information, visit ACL Emergency Preparedness.

items.title: Bureau of Indian Affairs Financial Assistance and Social Services (FASS)
items.summary: The Bureau of Indian Affairs offers financial assistance to American Indians and Alaska Natives who do not have access to TANF, do not qualify for TANF, or have used up their TANF lifetime limit. Help is secondary to other resources. Types of assistance include General Assistance, Child Assistance,…
items.html:
The Bureau of Indian Affairs offers financial assistance to American Indians and Alaska Natives who do not have access to TANF, do not qualify for TANF, or have used up their TANF lifetime limit. Help is secondary to other resources. Types of assistance include General Assistance, Child Assistance, Non-Medical Institutional or Custodial Care of Adults, Burial Assistance (up to $3,500), and Emergency Assistance (up to $1,500) for people whose homes were damaged or destroyed by fire, flood, or other disasters, to cover food, shelter, and utilities.

For more information, visit BIA Financial Assistance.

Contact: (202) 513-7642 or (202) 513-7622

items.title: SBA Disaster Loans for Businesses and Nonprofits
items.summary: The SBA’s Office of Disaster Recovery provides low-interest disaster loans to businesses of all sizes and private nonprofit organizations in declared disaster areas. Business Physical Disaster Loans: up to $2 million to repair or replace damaged real estate, machinery and equipment, inventory, and…
items.html:
The SBA’s Office of Disaster Recovery provides low-interest disaster loans to businesses of all sizes and private nonprofit organizations in declared disaster areas.

  • Business Physical Disaster Loans: up to $2 million to repair or replace damaged real estate, machinery and equipment, inventory, and other business assets.
  • Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL): working capital for small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, and most private nonprofits that suffered economic injury, even without property damage. The $2 million limit is shared with physical disaster loans.
  • Mitigation: borrowers may increase an approved physical damage loan to pay for improvements that reduce the risk of future damage.
  • Military Reservist Economic Injury Loans: help small businesses meet operating expenses when an essential employee is called to active duty.

For more information, visit SBA Disaster Assistance.

Contact: 1-800-659-2955 or disastercustomerservice@sba.gov. TTY users dial 7-1-1.
items.source: SAM.gov Assistance Listing 59.008 (published Feb. 4, 2026, downloaded Nov. 2026); https://www.sba.gov/about-sba/sba-locations/headquarters/office-of-disaster-recovery/ (snapshot 03)

items.title: USDA Business and Industry Loan Guarantees
items.summary: The Business & Industry (B&I) Guaranteed Loan Program guarantees loans made by private lenders to businesses in rural areas, so lenders can extend more credit. Eligible areas are generally outside cities and towns with more than 50,000 people. Lenders may request a guarantee for loans to for-profit…
items.html:
The Business & Industry (B&I) Guaranteed Loan Program guarantees loans made by private lenders to businesses in rural areas, so lenders can extend more credit. Eligible areas are generally outside cities and towns with more than 50,000 people. Lenders may request a guarantee for loans to for-profit businesses, nonprofits and cooperatives, federally recognized Tribes, public bodies, and individuals.

For more information, visit USDA B&I Loan Guarantees.

Contact: (202) 720-2600

items.title: USDA Disaster Assistance for Farmers
items.summary: USDA’s Farm Service Agency, Natural Resources Conservation Service, and Risk Management Agency offer programs to help producers prepare for and recover from natural disasters. Crop insurance is purchased through a private crop insurance agent; for other programs, contact your local USDA Service…
items.html:
USDA’s Farm Service Agency, Natural Resources Conservation Service, and Risk Management Agency offer programs to help producers prepare for and recover from natural disasters. Crop insurance is purchased through a private crop insurance agent; for other programs, contact your local USDA Service Center.

Visit farmers.gov Protection and Recovery to find programs that fit your situation, and sign up for USDA disaster email updates.

items.title: Crop Insurance
items.summary: Federal crop insurance protects agricultural producers against crop and revenue losses from natural causes. It is administered by USDA’s Risk Management Agency (RMA) and sold only through private crop insurance agents. To be covered, you must buy a policy for your crop by the sales closing date in…
items.html:
Federal crop insurance protects agricultural producers against crop and revenue losses from natural causes. It is administered by USDA’s Risk Management Agency (RMA) and sold only through private crop insurance agents. To be covered, you must buy a policy for your crop by the sales closing date in your county.

Find an agent with the RMA Agent Locator or learn more at RMA New York.

Contact: RMA Raleigh Regional Office (serves New York), (919) 875-4880, rsonc@usda.gov

items.title: Noninsured Crop Disaster Assistance Program (NAP)
items.summary: USDA’s Farm Service Agency (FSA) Noninsured Crop Disaster Assistance Program (NAP) pays producers of crops not covered by federal crop insurance when natural disasters cause low yields, loss of inventory, or prevented planting. Eligible crops include commercial crops grown for food, fiber, or…
items.html:
USDA’s Farm Service Agency (FSA) Noninsured Crop Disaster Assistance Program (NAP) pays producers of crops not covered by federal crop insurance when natural disasters cause low yields, loss of inventory, or prevented planting. Eligible crops include commercial crops grown for food, fiber, or bioenergy, as well as nursery and flower crops, Christmas trees, turfgrass sod, seed crops, and aquaculture. You must buy NAP coverage for the crop year before the loss occurs. Owners, landlords, tenants, and sharecroppers who share in the risk of producing the crop may qualify, subject to federal income limits.

For more information, visit farmers.gov or contact your local USDA Service Center.

Contact: FSA New York State Office, (315) 477-6300
items.source: SAM.gov Assistance Listing 10.451 (published Feb. 3, 2026, downloaded Nov. 2026); https://www.farmers.gov/protection-recovery (snapshot 05)

items.title: Emergency Farm Loans
items.summary: FSA’s Emergency Loan Program helps established family farmers and ranchers recover from losses in counties declared a disaster area by the President or designated by the Secretary of Agriculture (or under a USDA quarantine). Farms in neighboring counties also qualify. Funds may be used to restore…
items.html:
FSA’s Emergency Loan Program helps established family farmers and ranchers recover from losses in counties declared a disaster area by the President or designated by the Secretary of Agriculture (or under a USDA quarantine). Farms in neighboring counties also qualify. Funds may be used to restore or replace essential property, pay production costs for the disaster year, pay essential family living expenses, reorganize the farming operation, and refinance certain debts. Loans are available up to $500,000.

For more information, contact your local USDA Service Center or visit farmers.gov.
items.source: SAM.gov Assistance Listing 10.404 (published Feb. 2, 2026, downloaded Nov. 2026)
items.section: Help for Farmers and Agricultural Producers

items.title: Emergency Conservation Program (ECP)
items.summary: The Emergency Conservation Program shares the cost of emergency work to repair farmland damaged by floods, hurricanes, tornadoes, wildfires, and other natural disasters, to stop disaster-related soil erosion, and to conserve water during severe drought. Owners, landlords, tenants, and sharecroppers…
items.html:
The Emergency Conservation Program shares the cost of emergency work to repair farmland damaged by floods, hurricanes, tornadoes, wildfires, and other natural disasters, to stop disaster-related soil erosion, and to conserve water during severe drought. Owners, landlords, tenants, and sharecroppers who pay part of the cost of an approved practice in a disaster area may apply. Recent awards have ranged from $1,000 to $500,000. Funding depends on availability.

For more information, contact your local USDA Service Center or visit farmers.gov.
items.source: SAM.gov Assistance Listing 10.054 (published Feb. 3, 2026, downloaded Nov. 2026)

items.summary: Public Assistance reimburses governments and certain private nonprofits for disaster response costs and for permanent repairs to public infrastructure. Hazard Mitigation helps communities plan and carry out long-term projects that reduce future disaster damage to roads, bridges, and buildings. A…
items.html:
• Public Assistance reimburses governments and certain private nonprofits for disaster response costs and for permanent repairs to public infrastructure.
  • Hazard Mitigation helps communities plan and carry out long-term projects that reduce future disaster damage to roads, bridges, and buildings. A FEMA-approved hazard mitigation plan is required to receive mitigation funding.

For more information, visit NYS DHSES Disaster Recovery.

items.title: HUD Community Development Block Grant – Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR)
items.summary: When Congress appropriates special funding after major disasters, HUD awards Community Development Block Grant – Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) grants to states and local governments to help rebuild housing, infrastructure, and local economies, especially in low- and moderate-income areas. Residents…
items.html:
When Congress appropriates special funding after major disasters, HUD awards Community Development Block Grant – Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) grants to states and local governments to help rebuild housing, infrastructure, and local economies, especially in low- and moderate-income areas. Residents usually apply through the State or local program that receives the grant.

For more information, visit HUD CDBG-DR.

items.title: New York State Office of Emergency Management
items.agency: NYS Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services
items.summary: The New York State Office of Emergency Management (OEM), part of the Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services (DHSES), coordinates the activities of all State agencies to protect New York’s communities from natural and human-caused disasters. It supports local governments, voluntary…
items.html:
The New York State Office of Emergency Management (OEM), part of the Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services (DHSES), coordinates the activities of all State agencies to protect New York’s communities from natural and human-caused disasters. It supports local governments, voluntary organizations, and private industry with planning, response, technical support, and disaster recovery assistance.

  • To learn about available resources after a disaster, call 211 (outside New York City) or 311 (in New York City).
  • Sign up for free emergency alerts by phone, email, or text at NY-Alert.

For more information, visit NYS Office of Emergency Management.

Contact: DHSESPIO@dhses.ny.gov, (518) 242-5000
items.section: New York State and Local Resources

items.title: New York State Homes and Community Renewal Disaster Repair Programs
items.summary: After some major storms, New York State Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) has opened emergency repair programs, through local nonprofit partners, that help homeowners make primary residences safe and livable when insurance and other aid fall short. Past programs offered grants of up to $50,000…
items.html:
After some major storms, New York State Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) has opened emergency repair programs, through local nonprofit partners, that help homeowners make primary residences safe and livable when insurance and other aid fall short. Past programs offered grants of up to $50,000 based on income. These programs are announced after specific disasters.

Check Resilient NY Recovery Resources for current State recovery programs.

items.html:

items.title: Agricultural Research Basic and Applied Research
items.summary: ARS provides solutions to agricultural problems that affect Americans every day from field to table. We deliver scientific solutions to national and global agricultural challenges. We provide global leadership in agricultural discoveries through scientific excellence.
items.description: There are over 650 research and development projects being conducted by ARS scientists to deliver cutting-edge, scientific tools and innovative solutions for American farmers, producers, industry, and communities to support the nourishment and well-being of all people; sustain our nation’s agroecosystems and natural resources; and ensure the economic competitiveness and excellence of our agriculture. Our scientists frequently collaborate with research partners from universities, companies, other organizations, and other countries.
items.who: Those who may receive assistance and mutual interest cooperative agreements are described in 7 U.S.C. 3318 and whose primary purpose is conducting scientific research. Mutual interest Research Support Agreements are limited to only colleges and universities.
items.uses: Research and Development is conducted that is in cooperation with and is correlated with the Agricultural Research Service's in-house research programs and projects as defined by Congress.

items.title: Animal Disease and Animal Care
items.agency: Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service
items.summary: To protect U.S. agriculture from economically injurious animal diseases ensure the safety and potency of veterinary biologic, and ensure the humane treatment of animals. APHIS monitors and responds to potential diseases of livestock, wildlife, and invasive species as it strives to assure its stakeholders that it is on guard against the introduction or re-emergence of animal diseases that could limit agricultural…
items.description: APHIS' Veterinary Services program protects and improves the health, quality, and marketability of our Nation's animals, animal products, and veterinary biologics. Our team includes veterinary medical officers, animal health technicians, epidemiologists, statisticians, and many others in specialized fields.
items.who: Foreign, State, local, and U.S. Territorial government agencies, Indian Tribes, nonprofit institutions of higher education, and nonprofit associations or organizations requiring Federal support to eradicate, control, or assess the status of injurious plant and animal diseases and pests that are a threat to regional or national agriculture and conduct related demonstration projects.
items.uses: Conduct surveys, inspections to detect and appraise infestations, eradication and control activities, and carry out regulatory actions to prevent interstate spread of infestations and diseases.
